next_step: Capture loss notes, offer re-engagement in Q2 2025; security FAQ follow-up if procurement re-opens
notes:
Deal summary: Lost to OpenAI/Anthropic direct APIs. Key themes: brand simplicity, existing internal contracts, and a reorganized buyer team.

Recent timeline and touchpoints:
- 2024-06-12: inbound lead from Product (web form). AE assigned (Avery) same day.
- 2024-06-20: Intro call (30m) w/ Head of ML (L. Morales) + Eng manager. Heard: "We need something that just works and gets to users quickly."
- 2024-07-02: Demo (live) showing hosted API latency profiles, routing/fallback, and private deployment roadmap. Shared latency vs cost benchmarks (docs in Drive).
- 2024-07-18: POC kickoff meeting (Fireflies: ff_2024-07-18_OLYMPUS-demo-01). Agreed on 4-week POC: chat assistant on internal compliance docs + summarization. SE (Ravi) owned POC plan.
- 2024-08-05: Security questionnaire submitted (long list). Requested SOC2 report, KMS integration details, and residency options.
- 2024-08-20: POC mid-review: good quality, latency acceptable on dedicated pool. Engineering: "integration is straightforward but we need SSO and audit logs nailed down."
- 2024-09-10: Procurement team flagged cost sensitivity; asked for TCO vs direct APIs for 12-month run-rate. Provided Optimize recommendations and quantized cost scenarios.
- 2024-09-22: Internal re-org at RegSight. Primary champion (Head of ML) moved teams. Engagement cadence slowed.
- 2024-10-01: Procurement hardness: budget freeze for Q4. Procurement later indicated they'd choose fastest path to production once budget allowed.
- 2024-10-18: Received informal note: evaluating direct OpenAI/Anthropic APIs because "devs can ship faster and we already have internal token management with vendor contracts."
- 2024-10-30: Final check-in call. Customer verbally confirmed preference for direct vendor due to perceived lower integration friction and brand familiarity. No written RFP decision recorded.
- 2024-11-03: Marked closed-lost in CRM. Keys: champion left, budget freeze, comfort with direct API integration, and procurement preference for a single vendor contract.

Why we lost:
- Simplicity perception: Eng leadership repeatedly prioritized "fewest moving parts" and OpenAI had better-known SDKs for their stack.
- Brand comfort: Execs cited brand recognition and existing enterprise relationships as decision drivers.
- Internal churn: Reorg removed primary champion; successor had lower risk appetite.
- Timing/budget: Q4 freeze forced choice for minimal process stop-gap (direct APIs).
- Security friction: Security team asked many detailed items; while we had answers, the back-and-forth extended timeline and reinforced the "fastest ship" argument.

What we learned / next playbook items:
- Surface one-page migration path showing how a customer can start with hosted API and hybrid to private later; emphasize migration lift.
- Pre-schedule a SOC2 + KMS packet for enterprise prospects to shorten security cycles.
- Offer a limited-time pilot with billing credit that mirrors direct API price parity for first 3 months.
- Re-engage after Q2 hiring/re-org window; set reminder.

Quotes from stakeholders:
- "If we can get something up in two weeks with the least integration work, that's the preference." — Eng manager
- "We already have a blanket relationship with OpenAI for other teams; fewer procurement hoops." — Procurement lead

Immediate next steps recorded:
- AE to archive POC artifacts and share loss digest with RevOps and Product Sales (done).
- SE to submit suggested security packet template to enable faster turnarounds (in progress).
- Re-engage plan: Q2 2025 re-touch if budget re-opens and new champion identified.
